critical_code_review_comments: FIXED by testing agent: CompareContext.jsx had a race between load useEffect and save useEffect that wiped localStorage on first mount (save-effect ran with initial items=[] before setItems from load-effect took effect, deterministic under React 18 StrictMode). Refactored to lazy useState initializer reading from localStorage.

rca_of_the_issue: CompareContext used useState([]) + one useEffect to load from localStorage + another useEffect to save on items change. On first mount, both effects fire synchronously: load calls setItems(parsed) which schedules a re-render, but save immediately runs after with items still equal to [] and overwrites LS with '[]'. Under React 18 StrictMode double-invocation, the second pass then reads the wiped '[]' back into state. Fix: lazy-initialize useState from localStorage in one shot and remove the load-effect, so the save-effect never sees an uninitialized state.
